main_text.head: DISSERTATIO PHILOLOGICA
In Historiam Miraculosi Transitus Israelitarum per Mare Rubrum.
main_text.p: QUantoperè Judæorum Magistri in rebus ad fidem pietatemquè attinentibus à vero delirare, & nugaci §. 1.malèquè credulæ curiositati indulgere soleant, cùm omnia ipsorum in Sacris interpretamenta ut plurimùm inepta, traditiones fine fine modoquè malè consutæ &c. Tum vel præcipuè miraculorum, quæ creberrima olim in populo Dei contigerunt, enarrationes abundè satis fidem faciunt. Ea nimirum hominum illorum autadia, ea malè fana fingendi lubido, ut non contenti miraculis in Scriptura S. diserté memoratis חנם בתוך נם[?], ut loqui amant, miracula in miraculis comminiscantur: Inde mirabilibus nugamentis & absurdis pleraquè omnia sua scripta inferciunt. Id cum plurimis alijs, tùm nuperò didici experimentò. Cùm enim mihi, ut tum prælectionum ferebat ordo, enarranda essèt Historia Transitus Maris Rubri, ex cap. Exod. 14. Atque scirem diversum diversos de eo sentire, volupe fuit

page.notes: Woodcut border and initial are ornaments, not transcribed beyond the initial letter Q. The Hebrew phrase after "memoratis" is printed in a small line; it is read right to left as חנם בתוך נם, and the reading is uncertain, so it is marked [?]. The printed text has "essèt" (read as "esset"), and the printed "ef-fet" split is given as "essèt" with the accent kept as printed; check this word against the scan. The "§. 1." mark is a section mark in the left margin and is given as a note. Marks such as "Id cum plurimis" and the printed hyphens are kept as printed.
